Q: Why is `iota(0) | common` not a `random_access_range`? A:

iota(0) | take(2) is a random_access_range but not a sized_range, because iota(0) is not a sized_range.

take_view will only be a sized_range if the underlying range is a sized_range (Although it is theoretically possible to make iota(0) | take(2) a sized_range, this requires a paper because the standard library currently does not define the so-called infinity range).

When the underlying range of common_view is not random_access_range + sized_range, its begin()/end() returns a comon_iterator that wraps the underlying iterator/sentinel. Since common_iterator can only be forward_iterator at most, iota(0) | take(2) | common is just forward_range.

In C++20, to calculate the distance of ranges, there's no need to use std::distance which only applies common ranges; ranges::distance is sufficient and more powerful:

auto iota_2 = iota(0) | take(2);
auto dist = ranges::distance(iota_2); // gives 2

Q: 'Field required a bean of type that could not be found.' error Spring RESTful API using MongoDB A:

The class annotated with @SpringBootApplication should be in your root package (by default all classes in this package and subpackages are scanned) or you need to specify other packages (controller, entity and others) in @ComponentScan.

In order to create bean and inject it class in spring framework, Class should be marked with @Component, @Service or @Repository in class level accordingly. Make sure you have used it.
